correctness.rationale: On \(M=\Gamma\times\mathbb N\times\{\pm1\}\), write \(u_a(\gamma,k,s)=sr_k a_\gamma/2\) where \(r_k=k/(k+1)\), and translate by basepoint. Opposite-sign values approach but never attain the global extrema \(\pm\|a\|_\infty/2\), proving the isometry and strict local Lipschitz deficits. Independently reconstruct the equilateral Lipschitz-free predual as zero-sum \(\ell_1(M)\) with norm half its \(\ell_1\) norm; any normalized positive and negative mass measures meet only strict interior values and cannot attain the diameter. Finite evaluation identities characterize Y as the common kernel of weak-star continuous coordinate equations, so it is weak-star closed. For each k, paired coordinate differences /r_k recover a, and the resulting weak-star continuous projection has exact norm 1/r_k=(k+1)/k. A hypothetical weak-star norm-one projection would compose with a coefficient functional into a predual functional attaining norm at T(e_gamma), contradicting nonattainment. Hahn--Banach extends the limit on convergent sequences to a norm-one functional to provide an ordinary, non-weak-star continuous projection. Independent rational checks confirmed the first five projection constants. Infinite topology and norm-attainment conclusions are analytical, not consequences of these finite samples.
correctness.risk: Depends on the canonical Lipschitz-free weak-star topology, and explicitly chosen Y; no universal projection constant for all embeddings.

final_claim: For each infinite equilateral metric \(M\) of cardinality \(\kappa\), the real dual Lipschitz space has a weak-star closed isometric \(\ell_\infty(\kappa)\) subspace whose nonzero functions fail pointwise and Lipschitz-free functional norm attainment. Weak-star continuous projection norms onto that range have unattained infimum 1, approached exactly by explicit \((k+1)/k\) projections; an ordinary bounded norm-one projection does exist.
limitations: Real equilateral metric spaces only; one specific weak-star closed range.
Existence of ordinary norm-one projection uses noncanonical Hahn--Banach extension.
Finite computations do not prove infinite-dimensional weak-star statements; the analytic proof does.
